nodes.title: Building a triad from stacked thirds
nodes.whyImportant: A triad is three notes a third apart, so a student who can skip one letter at a time can build any chord on any note.

nodes.title: Major, minor, diminished and augmented triads
nodes.whyImportant: The size of each third decides whether a chord sounds bright, dark, tense or unstable, and Grade 5 asks for all four qualities.

nodes.title: Root, third and fifth
nodes.whyImportant: Naming the root, third and fifth is how a reader recognises a chord whatever order its notes are played in.

nodes.title: Root position and inversions
nodes.whyImportant: Which chord note is in the bass changes how solid a chord sounds and lets the bass line move by step.

edges.rationale: A triad is built by stacking thirds, so this is how every triad in the region is made.
The four triad qualities are what the triads backbone node asks a student to tell apart.
Inversions are the same triads with a different note in the bass.
Roman numerals name triads by the scale degree they stand on.
V7 is a triad with one more third stacked on top.
Playing a block chord is the triad as the hand meets it.
Every accompaniment pattern is a triad laid out in time.
The perfect cadence is the strongest of the cadences the backbone node covers.
The plagal cadence is one of the four cadences the backbone node covers.
The imperfect cadence is one of the four cadences the backbone node covers.
The interrupted cadence is one of the four cadences the backbone node covers.
The cadential six-four decorates V at a cadence.
Cadences are built from the primary chords I, IV and V.
A cadence is chord functions arriving: predominant, dominant, tonic.
Playing cadences is the backbone idea in the hands.
Choosing chords for a melody always ends with choosing its cadence.
A triad's quality is the size of the two thirds it is stacked from.
Stacking in thirds puts the root at the bottom, then the third, then the fifth.
An inversion is named by which member, root, third or fifth, is in the bass.
Each inversion has its letter and figures: a and 5/3, b and 6, c and 6/4.
The cadential six-four is named after the figures of a second-inversion chord.
A slash symbol such as C/E names a chord member as the bass.
Chord symbols spell the quality: m for minor, dim, aug.
The numerals of a major key name its seven triads.
The numerals of a minor key name its triads, with V made major.
The same degrees in major and minor carry different qualities.
Each degree of a major key has a fixed triad quality.
I, IV and V are the three major triads of a major key.
I, IV and V are the tonic, predominant and dominant.
ii does the same predominant job as IV.
Chord II joins I, IV and V as the fourth chord Grade 5 asks for.
In harmonic minor II is diminished, which is why IIb is used.
Numerals and chord symbols are two ways to name the same chord.
The seventh of V7 falls a step and its leading note rises.
The seventh makes the dominant pull harder to the tonic.
V7 in a minor key needs the raised leading note.
Resolving the seventh is voice leading: each note moves to the nearest note of the next chord.
Both end on I; the perfect cadence comes from V, the plagal from IV.
An imperfect cadence asks the question a perfect cadence answers.
Both start on V; the interrupted cadence swaps the expected I for vi.
A perfect cadence often uses V7 for a stronger close.
Ic - V - I is a common way to lead into a perfect cadence.
IIb - V is a common approach to an imperfect cadence.
In minor the interrupted cadence goes to a major VI.
Only chord notes need harmonising; passing notes are left out.
Most melodies at this level are harmonised with I, IV and V.
Once chords are chosen, smooth voice leading joins them.
A chosen chord becomes an accompaniment pattern under the melody.
Block chords make the quality of a triad heard and felt.
Playing inversions is the theory of inversions in the hand.
Broken chords are the simplest accompaniment pattern.
The same chord, played at once or spread out.
Playing I, IV and V in turn makes the primary chords familiar.
i - V in minor needs the raised seventh in the dominant.
The same tonic-dominant pull, in major and in minor.
The second passage ends on a perfect cadence.
The first passage ends on an imperfect cadence.
Both passages play V7 and resolve it.
The passages show the seventh resolving in real music.
Both passages play Ic - V7 - I.
ii - V - I puts chord ii before the dominant.
ii - V - I runs predominant, dominant, tonic.
The Alberti bass is one of the named accompaniment patterns.
The waltz bass is one of the named accompaniment patterns.
Stride and waltz basses are both a low note followed by a chord.
Stride and spread patterns are accompaniment patterns.
A melody over chords is a harmonised melody, played.
The Mozart passage puts its tune over an Alberti bass.
The Bach prelude moves its chords through inversions.

items.prompt: Which three white keys make the triad built on D?

answer.explanation: D, skip E, F, skip G, A: three notes a third apart.

wrong.explanation: D E F are next-door letters, steps rather than thirds, so they make a cluster, not a triad.
D to G is a fourth: G B D is the G chord with D added below, not a triad on D.
F♯ is a black key; the white-key triad on D uses F natural.

items.prompt: How many letter names are skipped between neighbouring notes of a root-position triad such as C E G?

answer.explanation: C (skip D) E (skip F) G: one letter is skipped each time, which is what makes a third.

wrong.explanation: Skipping no letters gives C D E, a run of steps rather than thirds.
Skipping two letters gives C F B♭, a stack of fourths, not a triad.

items.prompt: A triad has a major third at the bottom and a minor third on top. What quality is it?

answer.explanation: Major third below, minor third above, with a perfect fifth from root to top: a major triad.

wrong.explanation: A minor triad is the other way round: minor third below, major third above.
A diminished triad stacks two minor thirds, so its fifth is diminished.
An augmented triad stacks two major thirds, so its fifth is augmented.

items.prompt: Which of these triads is diminished?

answer.explanation: B to D and D to F are both minor thirds, and B to F is a diminished fifth.

wrong.explanation: C E G is major: a major third then a minor third.
A C E is minor: a minor third then a major third.
C E G♯ stacks two major thirds, so it is augmented.

items.prompt: What is the root of the chord E G C?

answer.explanation: Rearranged in thirds it is C E G, so C is the root even though E is lowest.

wrong.explanation: E is the lowest note here, but the bass note is not always the root: this is a C chord in first inversion.
G is the fifth of the chord once it is stacked in thirds as C E G.
Every triad has a root; stack the notes in thirds to find it.

items.prompt: What is the fifth of the F major triad?

answer.explanation: F major is F A C: F the root, A the third, C the fifth.

wrong.explanation: A is the third of F major, not the fifth.
F is the root of F major.
B♭ is a fourth above F and is not in the F major triad.

items.prompt: A C major chord has E as its lowest note. Which position is it in?

answer.explanation: With the third in the bass, a triad is in first inversion.

wrong.explanation: Root position needs the root, C, in the bass.
Second inversion has the fifth, G, in the bass.
Only a seventh chord has a third inversion, with the seventh in the bass.

items.prompt: Which spelling, lowest note first, is G major in second inversion?

answer.explanation: The fifth, D, is in the bass, with the root and third above: second inversion.

wrong.explanation: G B D has the root in the bass: root position.
B D G has the third in the bass: first inversion.
D F♯ A is a D major chord, not G major.

items.prompt: What does the label Ib mean?

answer.text: The tonic chord in first inversion
answer.explanation: The letter b marks first inversion, with the third in the bass.

wrong.text: The tonic chord in second inversion
wrong.explanation: Second inversion is labelled c, as in Ic.

wrong.text: The tonic chord with a flat
wrong.explanation: The b is a position letter, not a flat sign.

wrong.text: The tonic chord in a minor key
wrong.explanation: The letter shows the inversion, not the key; minor is shown by the chord itself.

items.prompt: Which figures describe a triad in second inversion?

answer.explanation: In second inversion the upper notes are a sixth and a fourth above the bass.

wrong.explanation: 5/3 is root position: a fifth and a third above the bass.
A lone 6 (short for 6/3) is first inversion.
A 7 marks a seventh chord, not a triad inversion.

items.prompt: Which chord is V in G major?

answer.explanation: The fifth degree of G major is D, so V is D F♯ A.

wrong.explanation: C is the fourth degree of G major, so C major is IV.
E minor is built on the sixth degree, so it is vi.
G major is the tonic chord, I.

items.prompt: In D major, which numeral names the chord G B D?

answer.explanation: G is the fourth degree of D major, so G B D is IV.

wrong.explanation: V in D major is built on A: A C♯ E.
ii in D major is E minor: E G B.
I in D major is D F♯ A.

items.prompt: In a major key, which degree carries the diminished triad?

answer.explanation: The triad on the leading note stacks two minor thirds, so vii° is diminished.

wrong.explanation: ii is minor in a major key.
iii is minor in a major key.
IV is major in a major key.

items.prompt: Which of these is a minor chord in F major?

answer.explanation: G minor (G B♭ D) is ii in F major.

wrong.explanation: B♭ major is IV in F major, a major chord.
C major is V in F major, a major chord.
F major is the tonic, I, a major chord.

items.prompt: In A minor, which chord is the dominant V used at cadences?

answer.explanation: The raised seventh, G♯, makes V major so that its leading note pulls up to A.

wrong.explanation: E G B uses the unraised seventh; at a cadence the dominant needs G♯.
D F A is iv in A minor, the subdominant.
C E G is III in A minor, built on the third degree.

items.prompt: What is chord iv in E minor?

answer.explanation: A is the fourth degree of E minor, and its triad is minor: A C E.

wrong.explanation: A C♯ E is A major; in E minor the C stays natural.
B D♯ F♯ is V in E minor, the dominant.
G B D is III in E minor.

items.prompt: What are the primary chords of C major?

answer.explanation: I, IV and V in C major are C, F and G.

wrong.explanation: D minor is ii, a secondary chord, not a primary one.

wrong.text: C, A minor and E minor
wrong.explanation: A minor and E minor are vi and iii, secondary chords.
This leaves out the tonic, C, which is always a primary chord.

items.prompt: In C major, which primary chord contains the note D?

answer.explanation: D is the fifth of G major (G B D), and it is in neither C E G nor F A C.

wrong.explanation: C major is C E G; D is not in it.
F major is F A C; D is not in it.
Neither I (C E G) nor IV (F A C) contains D.

items.prompt: Which chord pulls most strongly back to the tonic?

answer.explanation: V holds the leading note, which leans up to the tonic, so V wants to resolve to I.

wrong.explanation: IV leads away from home and usually moves on to V; its pull to I is gentler.
The tonic is home itself, so it has nowhere to resolve to.
iii shares two notes with I and has little pull of its own.

items.prompt: What job does chord ii usually do in a major key?

answer.text: A predominant that leads to V
answer.explanation: ii, like IV, prepares the dominant: ii - V - I is one of the commonest progressions.

wrong.text: A tonic substitute that ends pieces
wrong.explanation: Pieces end on I; ii does not give a sense of arrival.
ii has no leading note, so it cannot do the dominant job.

wrong.text: It is used only in minor keys
wrong.explanation: ii is common in major keys too, where it is a minor chord.

items.prompt: Which notes make chord II in C major?

answer.explanation: II is built on D, the second degree, and in C major it is minor: D F A.

wrong.explanation: F♯ is not in C major; II in C uses F natural.
C E G is the tonic chord, I.
G B D is the dominant, V.

items.prompt: In a minor key using the harmonic minor, what quality is chord II?

answer.explanation: In A minor II is B D F, two minor thirds: a diminished triad. That is why IIb, with D in the bass, is preferred.

wrong.explanation: ii is minor in major keys; in a minor key it is diminished.
B D F in A minor has a minor third and a diminished fifth, so it is not major.
The augmented triad in harmonic minor is III+, not II.

items.prompt: What are the notes of V7 in C major?

answer.explanation: V is G B D, and the seventh above G is F: G B D F.

wrong.explanation: G B D F♯ has a major seventh, which is not the dominant seventh and is not in C major.
C E G B♭ is a dominant seventh, but it is V7 of F major, not of C.
G B D is plain V; the seventh, F, is missing.

items.prompt: What are the notes of V7 in A minor?

answer.explanation: The dominant of A minor is E with the raised seventh, G♯, plus the seventh D.

wrong.explanation: Without G♯ there is no leading note, so the chord loses its pull to A.
A C E G is a seventh chord on the tonic, not the dominant.
D F A C is built on the subdominant.

items.prompt: When G7 resolves to C major, where does its seventh, F, usually go?

answer.explanation: The seventh of V7 resolves down by step, F to E, the third of the tonic chord.

wrong.explanation: Leaping or stepping the seventh upwards leaves it unresolved.
F is not in the C chord, so it cannot stay.
D is not in the C chord; the seventh moves to the nearest chord note below, E.

items.prompt: When G7 resolves to C major, where does the leading note, B, usually go?

answer.explanation: The leading note rises a semitone to the tonic.

wrong.explanation: A is not in the C chord, and the leading note wants to rise.
B is not in the C chord, so it has to move.
D is not in the C chord; the leading note goes to C, a semitone up.

items.prompt: Which two chords make a perfect cadence (called an authentic cadence in America)?

answer.explanation: A perfect cadence moves from the dominant to the tonic.

wrong.explanation: IV - I is the plagal cadence.
Ending on V makes an imperfect cadence.
V - vi is the interrupted cadence.

items.prompt: Which chords make a perfect cadence in F major?

answer.explanation: C is V of F major and F is I.

wrong.explanation: B♭ is IV of F major, so this is plagal.
I - V ends on the dominant: an imperfect cadence.
D minor is vi, so this is interrupted.

items.prompt: Which chords make a plagal cadence in G major?

answer.explanation: C is IV of G major and G is I.

wrong.explanation: D - G is V - I, a perfect cadence.
G - D ends on V, an imperfect cadence.
D - Em is V - vi, an interrupted cadence.

items.prompt: Which cadence is often called the "Amen" cadence?

answer.explanation: The IV - I close sung to "Amen" at the end of many hymns is plagal.

wrong.explanation: The perfect cadence is V - I.
An imperfect cadence ends on V, which does not sound final.
An interrupted cadence goes V - vi, a surprise rather than an Amen.

items.prompt: What makes a cadence imperfect (a half cadence in America)?

answer.explanation: Any phrase ending that rests on the dominant is imperfect, whatever chord comes before.

wrong.explanation: Ending on IV is not one of the four named cadences.

wrong.text: It goes from V to vi
wrong.explanation: V - vi is the interrupted cadence.

wrong.text: It is played out of time
wrong.explanation: The name is about the chords, not about how well it is played.

items.prompt: Which chords make an imperfect cadence in D major?

answer.explanation: IV - V ends on A, the dominant of D: imperfect.

wrong.explanation: A - D is V - I, a perfect cadence.
G - D is IV - I, a plagal cadence.
A - Bm is V - vi, an interrupted cadence.

items.prompt: Which chords make an interrupted cadence (a deceptive cadence in America) in C major?

answer.explanation: V goes to vi instead of the expected I.

wrong.explanation: G - C is V - I, a perfect cadence.
F - C is IV - I, a plagal cadence.
C - G ends on V, an imperfect cadence.

items.prompt: In A minor, an interrupted cadence goes from E major to which chord?

answer.explanation: In a minor key the submediant is major, so V - VI is E - F.

wrong.explanation: E - Am is V - i, a perfect cadence.
D minor is iv; E - Dm is not a named cadence.
C major is III; the interrupted cadence goes to VI.

items.prompt: In C major, a C major chord with G in the bass comes just before G - C at a cadence. What is it?

answer.explanation: I in second inversion over the dominant bass note, resolving to V: the cadential six-four.

wrong.explanation: Root position would need C in the bass; here the bass is G.
First inversion would have E in the bass.
IVb in C is F A C with A in the bass; this chord has no F.

items.prompt: What chord follows a cadential six-four?

answer.text: V in root position, on the same bass note
answer.explanation: The bass stays on the dominant while the upper notes fall to V.

wrong.explanation: Ic does not resolve straight to I; it leans on V first.
Ic is part of the dominant, so it moves on to V, not back to IV.
Ic leads to V; any vi would come after V, in an interrupted cadence.

items.prompt: Which notes does the chord symbol Dm stand for?

answer.explanation: The m means minor: D with a minor third, F, and a perfect fifth, A.

wrong.explanation: D F♯ A is D major, written plain D.
Adding C makes Dm7, which needs the 7 in the symbol.
D F A♭ has a diminished fifth: Ddim.

items.prompt: What does the symbol C/E mean?

answer.text: A C major chord with E in the bass
answer.explanation: The letter after the slash is the bass note: C major in first inversion.

wrong.explanation: The slash does not offer a choice.
C minor is written Cm.
The slash names one chord with a bass note, not two chords in turn.

items.prompt: Over a C major chord, a melody steps E - F - G with F on a weak beat. What is the F?

answer.explanation: F fills the gap between two chord notes, E and G, by step on a weak beat.

wrong.explanation: F is not in C E G.
An auxiliary note steps away and back to the same note, like E - F - E.
An appoggiatura falls on a strong beat, usually approached by leap.

items.prompt: Over a G major chord, a melody goes B - C - B with C on a weak beat. What is the C?

answer.explanation: C steps up from B and back to B: an auxiliary (neighbour) note.

wrong.explanation: A passing note goes on in the same direction to a different chord note.
C is not in G B D.
A suspension is held over from the chord before and falls on a strong beat.

items.prompt: In C major, a melody has A on a strong beat. Which primary chord fits it?

answer.explanation: A is the third of F A C, so IV harmonises it.

wrong.explanation: C E G does not contain A, so A would clash on a strong beat.
G B D does not contain A.

wrong.text: Any chord, because it is a strong beat
wrong.explanation: Strong-beat notes are the ones that must belong to the chord.

items.prompt: A melody in C major ends D - C. Which chords make a perfect cadence under it?

answer.explanation: D is in G B D and C is in C E G: V - I.

wrong.explanation: F A C does not contain D, and IV - I would be plagal.
This ends on V, and C E G does not contain D.
ii - I is not a perfect cadence; it needs V before I.

items.prompt: Moving from C major (C E G) to F major (F A C), which note can stay where it is?

answer.explanation: C is in both chords, so it can be held while the others move.

wrong.explanation: E is not in F A C; it moves up a semitone to F.
G is not in F A C; it moves up a step to A.
Leaping every note is harder to play and to hear; keep the common note.

items.prompt: Which motion between two parts is avoided in four-part harmony?

answer.explanation: Two parts moving in perfect fifths lose their independence, so harmony exercises avoid them.

wrong.explanation: Parallel thirds are smooth and common.
Parallel sixths are smooth and common.
Contrary motion, parts moving in opposite directions, is encouraged.

items.prompt: Which note order is an Alberti bass on a C major chord?

answer.explanation: Alberti bass goes lowest, highest, middle, highest.

wrong.explanation: C E G E is a plain broken chord going up and back, not the Alberti order.
Repeating one note is a drone or pedal, not a broken chord.
All three at once is a block chord.

items.prompt: What does a waltz left hand usually play in each bar of 3/4?

answer.text: A bass note on beat 1, then the chord on beats 2 and 3
answer.explanation: The low note marks the downbeat and the two chords give the lilt of the waltz.

wrong.text: The chord on beat 1, then bass notes on beats 2 and 3
wrong.explanation: This puts the weight in the wrong place; the bass marks beat 1.

wrong.text: One chord held for the whole bar
wrong.explanation: A held chord gives no waltz rhythm.

wrong.text: A bass note on every beat
wrong.explanation: A bass note on each beat is a walking line, not a waltz pattern.
